## Introduction

Both references were trained **without** one study (`params$holdout_study`, mumme_2023 by
default) and then used to label that study's cells:

- **SingleR:** `05_predict-holdout-singler.R`, with the `_no-<study>` trained reference.
- **scANVI:** `05_predict-holdout-scanvi.py`, scArches query mapping with the true labels hidden.

This notebook compares those predictions with the atlas labels. It only reads results, so it
re-knits quickly; produce them with `run-holdout-eval.sh`.

Things to keep in mind while reading:

- mumme_2023 contains the atlas's only 10x 5′ data. The held-out models therefore saw **no**
  5′ cells in training, so 5′ scores are a pessimistic lower bound for ScPCA SCPCP000007
  (all 10x v2 5′). Every metric is split by assay.
- mumme_2023 has no healthy donors.
- "Truth" is the atlas annotation, which is itself a prediction from the atlas authors.
- The main metrics use every cell, with SingleR's **unpruned** labels; the
  [confidence](#confidence) section looks at pruning and probability thresholds.

## Setup

```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
})

holdout_study <- params$holdout_study

root_dir <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_dir(".git"))
module_dir <- fs::path(root_dir, "analyses", "annotate-aml")
atlas_file <- fs::path(root_dir, "data", "AML-scAtlas", "AML_scAtlas_le29.h5ad")
holdout_dir <- fs::path(module_dir, "results", "holdout")
singler_file <- fs::path(holdout_dir, paste0("singler_predictions_", holdout_study, ".tsv"))
scanvi_file <- fs::path(holdout_dir, paste0("scanvi_predictions_", holdout_study, ".tsv"))

stopifnot(
  fs::file_exists(atlas_file),
  fs::file_exists(singler_file),
  fs::file_exists(scanvi_file)
)
```

Plot styling: color always identifies the **method** (categorical slots 1 and 2 of the
reference palette); assays are separate panels. Heatmaps use a single blue ramp.

```{r plot-style}
method_colors <- c(SingleR = "#2a78d6", scANVI = "#eb6834")
ink_primary <- "#0b0b0b"
ink_secondary <- "#52514e"
ink_muted <- "#898781"
grid_color <- "#e1e0d9"
seq_blue <- c("#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b")

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(color = ink_primary),
      axis.text = element_text(color = ink_secondary),
      axis.title = element_text(color = ink_secondary),
      strip.text = element_text(color = ink_primary, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = grid_color, linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification = "left",
      plot.title.position = "plot"
    )
)
scale_color_method <- scale_color_manual(values = method_colors, name = "Method")
```

## Load truth and predictions

True labels, assay and donor for the held-out cells, from the atlas subset (metadata only).

```{r truth}
adata <- anndataR::read_h5ad(atlas_file, as = "HDF5AnnData")
obs <- adata$obs
obs$cell_id <- adata$obs_names
rm(adata)

# label_fine -> label_broad map; each fine class belongs to exactly one broad class
label_map <- obs |>
  distinct(label_fine = as.character(label_fine), label_broad = as.character(label_broad))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(label_map$label_fine))

truth <- obs |>
  filter(Study == holdout_study) |>
  transmute(
    cell_id,
    donor_id = as.character(donor_id),
    sample = as.character(Sample),
    assay = as.character(assay),
    true_fine = as.character(label_fine),
    true_broad = as.character(label_broad)
  )

nrow(truth)
count(truth, assay)
```

Predictions from both methods, in one long table (one row per cell per method).

```{r predictions}
singler <- data.table::fread(singler_file, data.table = FALSE)
scanvi <- data.table::fread(scanvi_file, data.table = FALSE)

stopifnot(
  setequal(singler$cell_id, truth$cell_id),
  setequal(scanvi$cell_id, truth$cell_id)
)

predictions <- bind_rows(
  singler |> transmute(cell_id, method = "SingleR", pred_fine = singler_label),
  scanvi |> transmute(cell_id, method = "scANVI", pred_fine = scanvi_label)
) |>
  left_join(label_map, by = c("pred_fine" = "label_fine")) |>
  rename(pred_broad = label_broad) |>
  inner_join(truth, by = "cell_id") |>
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = names(method_colors)))

stopifnot(!anyNA(predictions$pred_broad))
```

Long format by label level, used by every metric below.

```{r long-levels}
by_level <- bind_rows(
  predictions |> transmute(cell_id, method, assay, donor_id,
                           level = "label_broad", truth = true_broad, pred = pred_broad),
  predictions |> transmute(cell_id, method, assay, donor_id,
                           level = "label_fine", truth = true_fine, pred = pred_fine)
) |>
  mutate(
    level = factor(level, levels = c("label_broad", "label_fine")),
    correct = truth == pred
  )
```

## Metric helpers

Per-label precision, recall and F1 within a group of cells. Labels are those present in the
truth for that group; precision counts every cell predicted as the label.

```{r metric-helpers}
per_label_metrics <- function(df) {
  labels <- unique(df$truth)
  purrr::map(labels, \(lab) {
    tp <- sum(df$truth == lab & df$pred == lab)
    n_true <- sum(df$truth == lab)
    n_pred <- sum(df$pred == lab)
    precision <- if (n_pred > 0) tp / n_pred else NA_real_
    recall <- tp / n_true
    f1 <- if (is.na(precision) || precision + recall == 0) 0 else
      2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
    tibble::tibble(label = lab, n_cells = n_true, precision, recall, f1)
  }) |>
    purrr::list_rbind()
}

label_metrics <- by_level |>
  group_by(method, assay, level) |>
  group_modify(\(df, key) per_label_metrics(df)) |>
  ungroup()
```

## Overall performance

Accuracy and macro-F1 (the unweighted mean of per-label F1, so rare labels count as much as
common ones) for each method, assay and label level.

```{r overall}
overall <- by_level |>
  group_by(method, assay, level) |>
  summarize(n_cells = n(), accuracy = mean(correct), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    label_metrics |>
      group_by(method, assay, level) |>
      summarize(macro_f1 = mean(f1), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("method", "assay", "level")
  )

overall |>
  arrange(level, assay, method) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r overall-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5}
overall |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(accuracy, macro_f1), names_to = "metric") |>
  mutate(metric = recode(metric, accuracy = "Accuracy", macro_f1 = "Macro-F1")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = assay, color = method)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_grid(level ~ metric) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
  scale_color_method +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Overall performance on held-out cells")
```

## Per-label performance

F1 for each label, by assay. Point size shows the number of true cells in that label, so
labels with few cells (noisy F1) are easy to spot.

```{r per-label-plot-function}
plot_per_label <- function(lvl) {
  df <- label_metrics |> filter(level == lvl)
  # order labels by mean F1 across methods and assays
  label_order <- df |>
    group_by(label) |>
    summarize(mean_f1 = mean(f1)) |>
    arrange(mean_f1) |>
    pull(label)
  df |>
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label_order)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = f1, y = label, color = method, size = n_cells)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.85) +
    facet_wrap(~assay) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 4, name = "True cells") +
    scale_color_method +
    labs(x = "F1", y = NULL, title = paste("Per-label F1:", lvl))
}
```

```{r per-label-broad, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
plot_per_label("label_broad")
```

```{r per-label-fine, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 8}
plot_per_label("label_fine")
```

Full per-label table:

```{r per-label-table}
label_metrics |>
  arrange(level, label, assay, method) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Confusion matrices

Rows are true labels and are normalized to sum to 1, so each row shows where that label's
cells went; a perfect method is a dark diagonal. Blank cells are 0. Only shares of at least
0.2 are labeled.

```{r confusion-function}
plot_confusion <- function(df, title) {
  label_levels <- sort(union(df$truth, df$pred))
  df |>
    count(method, assay, truth, pred) |>
    group_by(method, assay, truth) |>
    mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(
      truth = factor(truth, levels = rev(label_levels)),
      pred = factor(pred, levels = label_levels)
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = pred, y = truth, fill = share)) +
    geom_tile(color = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = ifelse(share >= 0.2, sprintf("%.2f", share), ""),
        color = share > 0.55
      ),
      size = 2.3,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = seq_blue, limits = c(0, 1), name = "Share of true label") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = ink_primary, `TRUE` = "#ffffff")) +
    facet_grid(assay ~ method) +
    labs(x = "Predicted label", y = "True label", title = title) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}
```

```{r confusion-broad, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9}
by_level |>
  filter(level == "label_broad") |>
  plot_confusion("Confusion matrix: label_broad")
```

At the fine level, one figure per method keeps the 28 labels readable.

```{r confusion-fine-singler, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 16}
by_level |>
  filter(level == "label_fine", method == "SingleR") |>
  plot_confusion("Confusion matrix: label_fine, SingleR")
```

```{r confusion-fine-scanvi, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 16}
by_level |>
  filter(level == "label_fine", method == "scANVI") |>
  plot_confusion("Confusion matrix: label_fine, scANVI")
```

## Per-donor accuracy

Overall accuracy for each donor and assay, to show how much performance varies across
donors. Donors with fewer than 100 cells in an assay are left out.

```{r per-donor, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
donor_accuracy <- by_level |>
  group_by(method, assay, level, donor_id) |>
  summarize(n_cells = n(), accuracy = mean(correct), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_cells >= 100)

donor_order <- donor_accuracy |>
  group_by(donor_id) |>
  summarize(mean_acc = mean(accuracy)) |>
  arrange(mean_acc) |>
  pull(donor_id)

donor_accuracy |>
  mutate(donor_id = factor(donor_id, levels = donor_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = accuracy, y = donor_id, color = method)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_grid(assay ~ level, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
  scale_color_method +
  labs(x = "Accuracy", y = NULL, title = "Accuracy by donor")
```

```{r per-donor-summary}
donor_accuracy |>
  group_by(method, assay, level) |>
  summarize(
    n_donors = n(),
    min = min(accuracy),
    median = median(accuracy),
    max = max(accuracy),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Confidence {#confidence}

### SingleR pruning

SingleR prunes (sets to `NA`) assignments whose score is an outlier for that label. How many
cells are pruned, and how accurate are the remaining labels?

```{r singler-pruning}
singler_pruning <- singler |>
  inner_join(truth, by = "cell_id") |>
  mutate(pruned = is.na(singler_pruned_label)) |>
  left_join(label_map, by = c("singler_label" = "label_fine")) |>
  rename(pred_broad = label_broad)

singler_pruning |>
  group_by(assay) |>
  summarize(
    n_cells = n(),
    frac_pruned = mean(pruned),
    acc_fine_all = mean(singler_label == true_fine),
    acc_fine_kept = mean((singler_label == true_fine)[!pruned]),
    acc_broad_all = mean(pred_broad == true_broad),
    acc_broad_kept = mean((pred_broad == true_broad)[!pruned])
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Which true labels are pruned most often?

```{r singler-pruning-by-label}
singler_pruning |>
  group_by(assay, true_fine) |>
  summarize(n_cells = n(), frac_pruned = mean(pruned), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(frac_pruned)) |>
  head(15) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

### scANVI probability threshold

If we only keep scANVI predictions whose maximum probability is at least a threshold, how do
accuracy and the fraction of cells kept change? (Two measures, so two panels.)

```{r scanvi-threshold, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
scanvi_conf <- scanvi |>
  inner_join(truth, by = "cell_id") |>
  left_join(label_map, by = c("scanvi_label" = "label_fine")) |>
  rename(pred_broad = label_broad)

thresholds <- seq(0, 0.95, by = 0.05)

threshold_curve <- purrr::map(thresholds, \(t) {
  scanvi_conf |>
    group_by(assay) |>
    summarize(
      threshold = t,
      frac_kept = mean(scanvi_max_prob >= t),
      label_fine = mean((scanvi_label == true_fine)[scanvi_max_prob >= t]),
      label_broad = mean((pred_broad == true_broad)[scanvi_max_prob >= t]),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}) |>
  purrr::list_rbind()

threshold_curve |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(frac_kept, label_fine, label_broad), names_to = "measure") |>
  mutate(
    panel = if_else(measure == "frac_kept", "Fraction of cells kept", "Accuracy of kept cells"),
    measure = recode(measure, frac_kept = "kept")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = threshold, y = value, linetype = measure)) +
  geom_line(color = method_colors[["scANVI"]], linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(panel ~ assay, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(label_broad = "solid", label_fine = "dashed", kept = "solid"),
    breaks = c("label_broad", "label_fine"),
    name = "Accuracy level"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Minimum max-probability", y = NULL, title = "scANVI: accuracy vs. confidence threshold")
```

## Malignancy proxy

The atlas's only per-cell malignancy signal is the `-like`/`LSC` HSPC sub-labels (see
`reference.md`). How often does each method call those cells `-like`/`LSC`, and how often
does it call other cells `-like`/`LSC`?

- **Sensitivity:** share of true `-like`/`LSC` cells predicted as any `-like`/`LSC` label.
- **False-positive rate:** share of other cells predicted as `-like`/`LSC`.

```{r malignancy-proxy}
is_malignant_like <- function(label) grepl("-like$", label) | label == "HSPC:LSC"

predictions |>
  mutate(
    true_mal = is_malignant_like(true_fine),
    pred_mal = is_malignant_like(pred_fine)
  ) |>
  group_by(method, assay) |>
  summarize(
    n_true_mal = sum(true_mal),
    sensitivity = mean(pred_mal[true_mal]),
    false_positive_rate = mean(pred_mal[!true_mal]),
    precision = sum(pred_mal & true_mal) / sum(pred_mal),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Where do the true `-like`/`LSC` cells go? (Rows sum to 1 within method and assay.)

```{r malignancy-proxy-detail}
predictions |>
  filter(is_malignant_like(true_fine)) |>
  count(method, assay, true_fine, pred_fine) |>
  group_by(method, assay, true_fine) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  slice_max(share, n = 3) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(true_fine, assay, method, desc(share)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
